title: Simple 3‑Day Full‑Body Gym Routine for NZ Beginners
meta_desc: Start a solid gym habit with this NZ‑focused 3‑day full‑body routine. Learn warm‑up, exercises, sets, reps, rest, cool‑down and pick the right NZ gym.
intro: If you’re new to the gym and can commit to three days a week, a full‑body program is the most efficient way to build strength and confidence. This guide walks you through a straightforward routine, the science behind the numbers, and how to choose a NZ gym that supports beginners.

sections.heading: Warm‑up – Get Your Body Ready
sections.body: A proper warm‑up raises your core temperature, improves joint mobility and reduces injury risk. Spend 5–10 minutes on low‑intensity cardio (treadmill walk, bike, or rowing) followed by dynamic stretches that mimic the movements you’ll perform in the workout.
list: 5 min brisk walk or easy jog on the treadmill

sections.heading: Full‑Body Workout – 3 Sessions per Week
sections.body: Perform the same circuit on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Using compound movements ensures you work multiple muscle groups in each session, maximising results while keeping the gym time under an hour. Choose a weight that lets you finish the prescribed reps with good form but feels challenging on the last two reps.

sections.heading: Sets, Reps & Rest – The Simple Math
sections.body: For beginners the classic 3 sets of 8‑12 reps balances strength and hypertrophy without overwhelming the nervous system. Rest periods are just long enough to recover but short enough to keep the heart rate up, aiding conditioning as a side benefit.
list: 8‑12 reps per set – aim for the higher end as you progress
If you can’t complete 8 reps, lower the weight; if you breeze through 12, add a few kilos

sections.heading: Cool‑down & Mobility
sections.body: Finishing with a cool‑down helps flush metabolic waste and improves flexibility. Spend 5‑10 minutes stretching the muscles you’ve just worked, holding each stretch for 20‑30 seconds. This routine also doubles as a quick mobility check for the next session.
list: Standing quad stretch – 20‑30 s each leg
Seated hamstring stretch – 20‑30 s each leg

sections.heading: Choosing a NZ Gym for Beginners
sections.body: Most major chains have at least one location with a dedicated free‑weight area and machines that suit the routine above. City Fitness offers 24/7 access and a strong community feel, while Anytime Fitness provides key‑card entry for early birds. Les Mills clubs often include group classes that can complement your strength days, and Jetts’ no‑contract model is handy if you’re still testing the waters. Don’t forget to check the Exercise NZ subsidised gym scheme – many participating clubs give 40‑70 % off membership for eligible adults, making a quality gym far more affordable.

sections.heading: Ready to Start?
sections.body: Now that you have a clear plan and know which gyms support beginners, take the next step and compare local options or find the perfect match for your lifestyle.
